definition: Mapping text across scripts (Arabic ↔ Latin) preserving pronunciation: proper names, Arabizi normalization, cross-lingual search.
details: Mapping text across scripts (Arabic ↔ Latin) preserving pronunciation: proper names, Arabizi normalization, cross-lingual search. Ambiguous in both directions (one Arabic name has many valid Latin spellings), so treated as a sequence modeling task, not a lookup table.

explainer.lead: Romanization maps text across scripts, such as Arabic to Latin, while preserving pronunciation, for uses like names, Arabizi normalization, and cross-lingual search. It matters because a plain lookup table fails when spellings vary.

tiers.eli5: It's like writing a name in English letters so someone who can't read the original script still knows how it sounds.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat it as a sequence modeling task rather than a dictionary mapping. A pitfall is ambiguity in both directions: one Arabic name has many valid Latin spellings.
tiers.paperLevel: It is mapping text across scripts preserving pronunciation, covering proper names, Arabizi normalization, and cross-lingual search; because it is ambiguous in both directions, it is treated as a sequence modeling task, not a lookup table.

explainer.example: The same Arabic name can be written several valid ways in Latin letters, so a model must handle the variants rather than match one spelling.
